# vvv

vvv is Vibe Vision Video. A VVV film is worth watching when the first three seconds give a reason to stay (faces, a shared memory, a question), something is always changing with nothing standing still longer than the template allows (usually 3 seconds), changes land on measured beats of the actual track, one thing is readable at a time and held long enough (about 5 seconds a page or more), each format is laid out for itself so 9:16 is not a crop of 16:9, the content is real and right (the user's photos, correct names, confirmed dates and events), and the sound is intended (music the user may use, at a sensible level, faded at the ends). Routes: Template (pick by purpose, then format, describe the template, add photos, arrange them, add and fit music, validate, sample, check, render, deliver); Recreation (fetch a reference video, measure its rhythm, write the page inventory before any code, rebuild from the inventory, compare frame by frame, never ship the reference itself); Brainstorm (pin down audience, placement, length, and one takeaway, offer three treatments, recommend one, sample its hardest scene first); Continue (resume an existing VVV project or render); and Open the package (verify a .vvv file first, then init, unpack, or add). Setup is the agent's job, not the user's: before the first project command of a session, run the doctor helper, which finds FFmpeg and reuses a Chrome Headless Shell the computer already downloaded.
